cases.question: How does UN R95 differ from UN R94 in impact direction?
cases.answer:
UN R95 is focused on side impact protection, with the mobile deformable barrier having a specific trajectory and speed, and various injury criteria such as chest deflection and abdominal force. [UN-ECE-R95 §Annex 4/2.4, p.24]

In contrast, UN R94 is concerned with frontal impact protection, involving an offset deformable barrier test to assess the safety of the front seats' occupants. [UN-ECE-R94 §3.1, p.9]

UN R95 specifies the propulsion of the mobile deformable barrier and its alignment with the impacted vehicle, ensuring a precise and controlled side impact test. [UN-ECE-R95 §Annex 5/6.2, p.36]

UN R94 details the requirements for the deformable barrier used in frontal impact testing, including its attachment to a mass and the dimensions of the barrier itself. [UN-ECE-R94 §Annex 9/5.1, p.48]

[Regulatory fact] The B-pillar is considered part of the vehicle structure for the purpose of testing Enhanced Child Restraint Systems. [UN-ECE-R129 §6.6.4.1, p.35]

[Regulatory fact] The deceleration time history of the structure shall be determined on the basis of the value of the longitudinal accelerometers at the base of the 'B' pillar on the struck side of the vehicle. [UN-ECE-R94 §Annex 3/6.1, p.28]

Engineering inferences
[Engineering inference] The design of the B-pillar must ensure it can withstand the forces exerted during side impact testing, including the potential for intrusion and deformation. [UN-ECE-R129 §6.6.4.1, p.35]

[Engineering inference] The B-pillar design should consider the requirements for the speed time history used in the test procedure, which is obtained from the longitudinal accelerometer at the 'B' pillar on the struck side. [UN-ECE-R94 §Annex 3/6.1, p.28]

UN R16 also includes relevant provisions on this topic. [UN-ECE-R16 §Annex 17/3.1, p.90]

cases.question: What requirements affect seat anchorage design?
cases.answer:
Relevant content on this topic was found in: UN R16.

Regulatory facts
[Regulatory fact] The seat anchorage is defined as the system by which the seat assembly is secured to the vehicle structure, including the affected parts of the vehicle structure. [UN-ECE-R16 §2.14.6, p.9]

[Regulatory fact] The seat anchorage design must accommodate the ISOFIX top tether anchorage and ensure it remains accessible. [UN-ECE-R16 §Annex 17/3.1, p.90]

[Regulatory fact] A technical description of the seat anchorages and belt anchorages, including drawings and specifications of the materials used, is required for the approval of the restraint system. [UN-ECE-R16 §3.2.2.1, p.12]

Engineering inferences
[Engineering inference] The seat anchorage must be designed to secure the seat assembly to the vehicle structure, considering the affected parts of the vehicle structure, which implies that the anchorage should be strong and durable enough to withstand various loads and stresses. [UN-ECE-R16 §2.14.6, p.9]

[Engineering inference] The design of the seat anchorage should consider the vehicle structure and the seat structure, including the adjustment system and attachments, to ensure a secure and stable connection, which may involve the use of reinforcements and specific materials. [UN-ECE-R16 §3.2.2.1, p.12]

cases.question: What requirements affect the driver's seat design?
cases.answer:
Relevant content on this topic was found in: UN R94, UN R16.

Regulatory facts
[Regulatory fact] The driver's seat must be equipped with a safety-belt reminder satisfying the requirements of this Regulation. [UN-ECE-R16 §8.4.1, p.36]

[Regulatory fact] The seat shall be regarded in its most forward driving or travelling position appropriate to the dimensions of the manikin for the assessment of certain requirements. [UN-ECE-R16 §7.7.1.5, p.29]

[Regulatory fact] For seats capable of being turned to or placed in other orientations, the requirements of paragraph 8.1.1. shall only apply to those orientations designated for normal use when the vehicle is travelling on a road. [UN-ECE-R16 §8.1.10, p.34]

[Regulatory fact] Vehicles of category N1 of a total permissible mass exceeding 2,250 kg but not exceeding 2,500 kg are deemed to meet the requirements of paragraph 5, where their structural basis is a ladder frame and the requirements of UN Regulation No. 137 are fully complied with and at least one of the following conditions is met. [UN-ECE-R94 §5.3.2, p.16]

Engineering inferences
[Engineering inference] The driver's seat design must consider the interaction with the safety-belt reminder system and ensure it meets the requirements of the Regulation. [UN-ECE-R16 §8.4.1, p.36]

[Engineering inference] The driver's seat design should consider the seating position and orientation to ensure compliance with the Regulation's requirements for safety-belt reminders and seat orientation. [UN-ECE-R16 §8.1.10, p.34]

[Engineering inference] The driver's seat design must consider the vehicle's category and mass to ensure compliance with the Regulation's requirements for seat and safety-belt interaction. [UN-ECE-R94 §5.3.2, p.16]

cases.question: How does UN R16 relate to UN R94?
cases.answer:
UN R16 applies to vehicles of categories M, N, O, L2, L4, L5, L6, L7 and T with regard to the installation of safety-belts and restraint systems [UN-ECE-R16 §1.1, p.5]

UN R94 applies to vehicles of category M1 with a total permissible mass not exceeding 3,500 kg and to vehicles of category N1 with a total permissible mass not exceeding 2,500 kg [UN-ECE-R94 §1, p.5]

UN R94 protects occupants of the front seats in the event of a frontal collision [UN-ECE-R94 §3.1, p.9]

The edge of the strip should be located no more than 5 mm above the base of the upper barrier-mounting flange, or 5 mm below the top of the lower barrier-mounting flange. Five clearance holes of 9.5 mm diameter must be drilled in both strips to correspond with those in the mounting flange on the barrier (see paragraph 4. above). None of the fixtures shall fail in the impact test. In the case where the deformable barrier is mounted on a load cell wall (LCW) it should be noted that the above dimensional requirements for mountings are intended as a minimum.
